{\LARGE\bfseries\sffamily\color{AtlasNavy} Strongly convex noisy value optimization with Schatten-Lipschitz Hessians and no curvature upper bound\par}\vspace{5pt}


\textbf{Setting ID.} \texttt{SO\_\allowbreak{}ZO\_\allowbreak{}N10\_\allowbreak{}schatten\_\allowbreak{}hessian\_\allowbreak{}gaussian}



Single-objective optimization



The full Schatten range p from two to infinity parameterizes Hessian regularity under independent Gaussian scalar values. The risk comparison separates large-budget asymptotics from all-budget lower bounds.



\textbf{Status.} Bounds missing



\textbf{TASK tags.} solution concept: Strongly convex minimization; task family: Single objective



\textbf{MODEL tags.} convexity: Strongly convex; smoothness: Lipschitz Hessian



\textbf{ORACLE tags.} feedback quality: Stochastic gaussian; operation: Function value; public information: Hidden objects explicitly declared; public information: Public inputs explicitly declared; scalar derivative order: Scalar function value (order 0)



\textbf{ALGORITHMS tags.} randomization: Private randomness allowed; restriction: No additional span restriction explicitly imposed



\textbf{GUARANTEE tags.} mode: Expectation; quantifier: Algorithm before instance; randomness: Algorithm private seed



\textbf{RESOURCE tags.} budget: Fixed worst-case budget; measure: N noisy value



\needspace{7\baselineskip}\section{1. Setting specification}


\needspace{4\baselineskip}\subsection{Task}


Minimize a hidden strongly convex objective globally on \AtlasInlineMath{\mathbb R^d} using noisy scalar values, with terminal objective error as the loss.



\needspace{4\baselineskip}\subsection{Admissible model}


For \AtlasInlineMath{p\in[2,\infty]}, \AtlasInlineMath{f:\mathbb R^d\to\mathbb R} is \AtlasInlineMath{C^2} and satisfies
\AtlasMath{\nabla^2 f(x)\succeq\mu I,\qquad\|\nabla^2f(x)-\nabla^2f(y)\|_{S_p}\le\rho\|x-y\|_2}
 for every \AtlasInlineMath{x,y\in\mathbb R^d}. The unique global minimizer obeys \AtlasInlineMath{\|x_*\|_2\le R}.



The Schatten norm \AtlasInlineMath{\|A\|_{S_p}} is the ell-p norm of the singular values, with \AtlasInlineMath{S_2} the Frobenius norm and \AtlasInlineMath{S_\infty} the operator norm. There is no global upper bound on the Hessian or gradient. The known minimizer ball does not constrain queries or output.



\needspace{4\baselineskip}\subsection{Oracle interface}


One query at any \AtlasInlineMath{x_t\in\mathbb R^d} returns \AtlasInlineMath{Y_t=f(x_t)+\xi_t}, where the noises are fresh independent \AtlasInlineMath{N(0,1)} variables, independent of the algorithmic seed and past observations. Opposite-point observations have independent noise; no same-sample reuse or noiseless values are available.



Public inputs are \AtlasInlineMath{d,p,\mu,\rho,R} and a horizon \AtlasInlineMath{T} or target error \AtlasInlineMath{\varepsilon}. The objective is hidden.



\needspace{4\baselineskip}\subsection{Output}


Return any measurable \AtlasInlineMath{\widehat x\in\mathbb R^d} from the transcript, whether or not it was queried.



\needspace{4\baselineskip}\subsection{Loss or accuracy criterion}


The base loss is \AtlasInlineMath{f(\widehat x)-f(x_*)}. For a fixed horizon, the minimax risk is
\AtlasMath{\mathcal E_T^{(p)}=\inf_A\sup_{f\in\mathcal F_{S_p}(d,\mu,\rho,R)}\mathbb E[f(\widehat x)-f(x_*)].}
 Expectation includes private randomization and observation noise.



\needspace{4\baselineskip}\subsection{Resource accounting}


Each scalar noisy value costs one evaluation. Repeated values, every side of a finite difference, localization, and validation are all charged. The algorithm uses at most \AtlasInlineMath{T} evaluations on every execution. Exact specification of finite query coordinates, arithmetic, and storage are free.



\needspace{4\baselineskip}\subsection{Algorithm views and success guarantees}


Queries, stopping decisions, and the output are measurable functions of the preceding transcript and an instance-independent private random seed. The unknown instance is fixed before the seed is realized. No span, support, zero-respecting, or memory restriction is imposed.



Internal exact-real computation and storage using public inputs and received information are uncharged. The stated budget must hold on every execution path.




\AtlasMath{\forall f:\ \mathbb E[f(\widehat x)-f(x_*)]\le\varepsilon}




The expectation averages the independent Gaussian observations and private randomization after the function is fixed. The evaluation count is capped on every path.



\textbf{Budget convention.} fixed\_worst\_case

\AtlasInlineMath{\rho}: Schatten-p Hessian Lipschitz modulus \textbf{Domain:} \AtlasInlineMath{\rho>0}.



\AtlasInlineMath{R}: Known Euclidean radius of the minimizer \textbf{Domain:} \AtlasInlineMath{R>0}.

Any sufficiently large threshold supplied by Theorem thm:schatten after universal multiplicative constants are fixed. No explicit dimension dependence is asserted.
